readmeText:
Claude Plugins

 Anthropic's own plugins for Claude, and the claude-plugins-official marketplace for Claude Code.

 Submitting a plugin? Submit it at claude.ai/directory/manage . Plugins accepted there are served across Claude products. Pull requests to this repository are not monitored.

 What is changing

- All plugins are now submitted at claude.ai/directory/manage , and are served across Claude products from there.

- .claude-plugin/marketplace.json is being phased out for third-party plugins. It will be reduced over time to Anthropic's own plugins.

- This repository is the home of Anthropic's own plugins. Its checks cover the plugin folders here, not the plugins hosted in other repositories.

 ⚠️ Important: Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

 Structure

- /plugins - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic

- /external_plugins - Third-party plugins added before submissions moved to claude.ai/directory/manage , and Anthropic's channel plugins (Discord, fakechat, iMessage and Telegram)

 Installation

 Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

 To install, run /plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official

 or browse for the plugin in /plugin > Discover

 Contributing

 Third-party plugins

 Submit and manage your plugin at claude.ai/directory/manage . Do not open a pull request here: pull requests are not monitored, and marketplace.json is being reduced to Anthropic's own plugins.

 Anthropic plugins

 Plugins in /plugins are developed by Anthropic team members. See /plugins/example-plugin for a reference implementation. Every folder there is checked on each pull request, whether or not marketplace.json lists it.

 Plugin Structure

 Each plugin follows a standard structure:

 plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│ └── plugin.json # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/ # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/ # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/ # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md # Documentation

 Plugin names are immutable

 The name field in a marketplace entry is an immutable slug . Once a plugin has been published, its name must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a plugin-not-found error.

- To change how a plugin is labeled in the UI, set or update displayName instead.

- If a rename is genuinely unavoidable, add an entry to the top-level renames map in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json so existing installs auto-migrate:

 "renames" : {
 "old-name" : " new-name "
}

 The Claude Code plugin loader reads this map and transparently rewrites the old slug to the new one on the user's next sync.

 Skill-bundle plugins

 When a plugin's source repository ships skills ( SKILL.md files) without a .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest, the marketplace entry can declare the skills directly using strict: false and an explicit skills array.

 {
 "name" : " example-bundle " ,
 "description" : " Brief description of the bundled skills. " ,
 "author" : { "name" : " Author Name " },
 "category" : " development " ,
 "source" : {
 "source" : " git-subdir " ,
 "url" : " https://github.com/example-org/sdk.git " ,
 "path" : " packages/agent-skills " ,
 "ref" : " main " ,
 "sha" : " <commit sha> "
 },
 "strict" : false ,
 "skills" : [
 " ./skill-a " ,
 " ./skill-b " ,
 " ./skill-c "
 ],
 "homepage" : " https://github.com/example-org/sdk "
}

 Each path in skills is relative to source.path and points at a directory containing a SKILL.md . Paths can reach deeper than a single level — for example, ["./libA/skill-1", "./libB/skill-2"] exposes a curated subset across multiple library subdirectories. Each skill is registered as <plugin-name>:<skill-name> in Claude Code.

 For the underlying schema, see Strict mode in the marketplace documentation.

 License

 Please see each linked plugin for the relevant LICENSE file.

 Documentation

 For more information on developing Claude Code plugins, see the official documentation .

 REA: Reverse Engineer Anything

 One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.

 See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level.

 Website · Guides · Showcases

 Quick start · How REA works · What you can analyze · Showcases · Build RL environments · FAQ · Documentation

 npx rea-agents setup

 Important
 Get REA from morluto/rea ,
 rea.tools , or the rea-agents npm package .
Follow the installation and release links from these official sources. A similar
repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official.

 Join the Reverse Engineering Community

 Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

 See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project.

 REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion.

 Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine.

 Visit the REA website for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies.

 Quick start

 On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron
analysis require a procps-compatible ps on REA's PATH for process ownership
checks. Recovery steps are in docs/getting-started/installation.md under
"Linux owned-process prerequisite".

 Set up your agent

 With Node.js and npm installed, run:

 npx rea-agents setup

 Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds
REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing
configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup records the selected runtime and REA
entry script directly. If acquired through a package runner, keep its cache entry
available. Run package acquisition from a trusted directory outside the target
project. Installation and recovery details are in the setup guide below.

 Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and
 other agents . See
 installation and setup for provider configuration,
manual MCP registration, Claude Code/Codex plugins, and the Cursor Marketplace
plugin.

 MCP uses compact input schemas by default to reduce context overhead. Set
 REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full in your MCP registration when you need the
complete advertised field guidance and nested validation details. Both profiles
keep the full tool set and canonical server validation. See
"Compact input schema profile" in the MCP contracts guide.

 Complete output schemas are advertised by default. If your client caps the
complete tools/list frame, set REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact to
bound each advertised output schema, or off to omit output schemas entirely.
Both settings keep canonical server-side validation and complete structured
results. See "Output schemas" in the MCP contracts guide.

 Ask your agent

 Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a
similar feature for my project.

 Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand.

 Use the terminal

 Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR:

 npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json

 The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence.
Replace the path with your target, such as "D:/apps/example" on Windows.

 To install the rea command for regular use:

 npm install --global rea-agents
rea --help

 For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the
 CLI and Evidence guide for native commands, provider selection,
snapshots and scripting.

 Update REA

 REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your
installation up to date.

 For a CLI installed with npm install --global or bun add --global :

 rea update

 rea --update is an alias for this verified workflow and accepts the same global
output flags. Use rea update when combining it with other command controls.

 Updater commands retain at most 4 MiB of stdout and stderr combined. Oversized
metadata replies are rejected after the command exits; verbose installs continue
with bounded diagnostics. Human progress output respects terminal backpressure
and waits for submitted writes to finish.

 Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release,
upgrade Bun manually before running rea update .

 To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed
by the update.

 If you use npx , update your agent setup with:

 npx rea-agents@latest setup

 Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands,
use npx rea-agents@latest followed by the command. With Bun, use
 bunx rea-agents@latest in place of npx rea-agents@latest .

 How REA works

 Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code.
REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up
questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation.
CLI commands use the same workflows.

 Open the full-size figure .

 What you can analyze

 REA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.23.4), 24.x (>=24.22.1), or 26.12.1+, plus npm.
Additional tools and host support depend on the target:

 Target
 What REA returns

 Desktop installations

 Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references

 Built-in static JSON inspection; Apple IPS

 Validation, sections, exact import/export WAT forms and decoded WAT

 Local database/WAL snapshot; Node.js 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ with native SQLite limits

 Caller-supplied pwntools on Linux x64; optional GDB/pwndbg; recorded crashes

 JavaScript / Electron

 Websites

 Saved network captures

 Manifest declarations, classes, decompiled methods and references
 Headless JADX and a full JDK on Linux/macOS/Windows x64; Android guide

 Caller-supplied adb (emulator or hardware); ADB guide

 Engine-backed project units, artifact digests and type/method pseudo-code
 A caller-started JEB client serving MCP, selected with REA_JEB_MCP_URL; JEB guide

 Endpoints, DNS, TLS SNI, protocol distribution and HTTP requests

 Artifact and JavaScript guide , Apple applications

representativeRepos.readmeText:
security-audit

 A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

 This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness . The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

 What it does

 The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

- Reconnaissance -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json .

- Coverage-led hunting -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.

- Candidate validation -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.

- Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .

- Independent record verification -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.

- Target-neutral reporting -- derive REPORT.md , FINDINGS-DETAIL.md , and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md from the verified records and coverage ledger.

 The parent runs validate-coverage-ledger.cjs after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs validate-findings.cjs in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

 The verdicts are distinct: confirmed has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, needs_validation has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and rejected records a disproved candidate.

 Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

 Files

 File
 Purpose

 SKILL.md
 Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns

 RECONNAISSANCE.md
 Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions

 HUNTING.md
 Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules

 ATTACK-CLASSES.md
 Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts

 MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md
 Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets

 AI-AND-LLM.md
 Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets

 WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md
 HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets

 CLIENT-SIDE.md
 DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets

 SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md
 Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes

 CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md
 IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes

 PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md
 RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes

 RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md
 Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes

 DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md
 Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes

 DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md
 Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes

 VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md
 Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting

 report-schema.json
 JSON schema for all three findings.json verdicts

 validate-findings.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for findings.json in Phases 4 and 5

 validate-findings.test.cjs
 Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks

 validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for coverage-ledger.json in Phases 1–5

 validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
 Coverage-ledger validator tests

 Installation

 Install the skill with the Skills CLI :

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit

 Use --global for a user-level installation:

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit \
 --global

 Run npx skills --help for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

 Usage

 Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

 security audit this codebase

 find security vulnerabilities in ./src

 do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

 The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> . The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

 Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents

- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators

- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as needs_validation instead of executing target code.

 Design principles

- Only confirm established boundary failures. Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as needs_validation with its exact unresolved fact.

- Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

- Severity requires impact. Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.

- Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities. If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.

- Multiple runs improve coverage. In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

 Contact

 Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

representativeRepos.readmeText:
T3 Code

 The open-source control plane for coding agents.

 Download ·
 iOS ·
 Android ·
 Web ·
 Docs ·
 Discord

 T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone.

 It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it.

 What you get

- Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to.

- Every agent in one place. Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex.

- Desktop, web, and phone. One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android.

- Remote ready. Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect .

- Git built in. Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button.

- Fast. Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug.

- Open. MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it.

 Install

 Desktop app

 Download T3 Code for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager:

 Platform
 Command

 macOS
 brew install --cask t3-code

 Windows
 winget install T3Tools.T3Code or scoop install extras/t3code

 Arch Linux
 yay -S t3code-bin

 Nix
 nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code

 Debian, Ubuntu
 .deb from Releases

 Command line

 This installs the t3 command. Run t3 to start the server and open the web app.

 curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

 On Windows, in PowerShell:

 irm https: // t3.codes / install.ps1 | iex

 To try it once without an install, run npx t3@latest .

 Phone

 Get the app from the App Store or Google Play . Then follow remote access to connect it to your computer.

 Sign in to an agent

 T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install Claude Code and run claude auth login , or install Codex CLI and run codex login .

 Provider setup has the steps for each agent. Install T3 Code covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS.

 "Wait, what are you selling me?"

 Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

 We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want.

 Documentation

- Install and first run

- Remote access from a phone or another machine

- Permission modes

- Source control

- Connect outside agents over MCP

- FAQ

 All docs has the full list.

 Contributing

 We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first.

- Read CONTRIBUTING.md before you report a bug or open a pull request.

- Put feature requests in Ideas .

- Build from source with the development runbook . The architecture overview explains how it works.

- Get help in Discord .

 License

 MIT

 Strategic sponsors  

   ·   Special sponsor  

 Demo workspace · Default dark theme · Watch the HD tour

 What you can do

 Voice cloning

 Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice.

 Video dubbing

 Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original.

 Voice design

 Describe a voice in words and generate it.

 Local models

 Choose your engines and download only the models you need.

 More screenshots

 Workspace overview

 Model packs

- Dictate & transcribe — A floating dictation widget and local transcription

- Narrate & batch — Stories, audiobooks and queued jobs

- Connect & automate — Local API, MCP, reusable recipes and watch folders

 Start with VoiceStudio (default, powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice), or pick from dozens of other engines in the Model Manager. See the features & engine catalog .

 Pro and Cloud

 Everything above is free, runs on your own hardware and needs no account. Pro and Cloud are optional.

    VoiceStudio Pro

 For paid client work across more than one machine.

 - A Commercial License for your client work, emailed to you

 - One user on up to 3 devices at once

 - Send jobs to your other GPUs while your projects stay local

 - New features and fixes first

 Closed-source build, account required, 7-day full refund. The AGPL-3.0 app stays free, including commercial use under its terms.

 See Pro plans →

    VoiceStudio Cloud

 A hosted voice and dubbing API, coming soon. No GPU needed.

 - Speech, voice design and voice cloning with consent

 - Dubbing, transcription and audiobooks

 - Usage and credits by day or project

 - Long jobs that run on their own

 Not available yet: join early access for free usage credits. The desktop app stays free and local.

 Join Cloud early access →

 Platforms

 Experimental Windows ROCm setup supports selected RDNA 2 RX 6000 GPUs with targets gfx1030 , gfx1031 or gfx1032 ; RX 6500 XT ( gfx1034 ) is excluded. GPU transcription uses a CTranslate2 build with native
 gfx1031 kernels that this repository builds from upstream source and pins by
hash, and setup checks actual GPU kernel execution. RX 6700 XT tests also cover native Torch speech generation and
PyTorch Whisper. ROCm 10 faster-whisper uses a separate inference process to
preserve safe CPU selection and fallback. Other cards and workloads retain the qualification limits in the guide.
Performance presets validate changed engine selections in an offline child
process before saving them, preserving fallback when an installed runtime fails.

 Choose your system, then expand an installation method.

 Native GGUF engines additionally support engine-specific Vulkan acceleration on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs ( OmniVoice , CosyVoice ). OmniVoice GGUF selects its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux. Vulkan discovery retries a stalled hidden probe with a native summary; Windows and Linux desktop builds fail rather than silently ship without their Vulkan module.

 NVIDIA, AMD ROCm and Compose instructions

 iPhone / iPad · IPA · sideloading

 iOS / iPadOS 17+ · Preview · On-device, offline after model download.

 Download · Guide

 Desktop and phone installers are on the latest release ; Docker images come from GHCR. No GPU? The app is fully usable on the CPU, just slower. Native GGUF engines can also use Vulkan on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs; OmniVoice GGUF picks its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux ( OmniVoice , CosyVoice ). Speed by engine and hardware: performance .

 Get started

 Install using the options above. Then open Voice cloning , pick a voice or add a clean reference recording, type your text and generate. The app asks before it downloads any model.

 More install options : a specific version, current main, uninstall, from source, with a coding agent
 curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --version X.Y.Z # a specific release
curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --main # build current main
curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --uninstall # remove the app, keep your data

 If voicestudio.sh is unreachable, run the script straight from the repository:
 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/main/scripts/install.sh | sh .
Prerequisites and behavior: installer guide .

 From source

 git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git
 cd VoiceStudio
bun run dev

 bun run dev installs the JavaScript dependencies and, when using a supported
local backend, the Python dependencies before launching Electron. Run
 bun run setup:api directly when you only need to rebuild the Python environment.

 HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows.

 The HyperFrames Studio app is free to use as well; its Pro plan adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models.

 Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run npx hyperframes skills update once, then ask your agent to make a video.

 Quick Start

 With an AI coding agent

 For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin:

 claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes
claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes

 To enable auto-update for the hyperframes marketplace, run claude in a
terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run /plugin , then select
 Marketplaces → hyperframes → Enable auto-update . Afterward, use
 /hyperframes:hyperframes . See the plugin guide
for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration.

 For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use:

 npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

 The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the Core Skills group is all you need; /slideshow , /remotion-to-hyperframes and /figma install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), npx hyperframes skills update installs exactly the core set, whereas skills add --all installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under .claude/skills / .agents/skills are excluded by default. For the full published set use npx hyperframes skills .

 skills add resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag main by hours. npx hyperframes skills update installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them.

 Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames
checkout, use npx hyperframes skills update for a global install instead: a
project-local installer target can overlap the tracked skills/ source and
overwrite uncommitted edits. See contributor setup .

 Try a prompt like:

 Using /hyperframes , create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music.

 The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills.

 Skills

 HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the /hyperframes skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first.

 For standalone installation, default to the core set ( /hyperframes , /hyperframes-cli , /hyperframes-registry , /media-use , /reverse-any-video , /style-sampling ). npx hyperframes skills update installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker ( npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without --skill installs all 9. Use npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill <name> for just one (bare name, no leading / ).

 Standalone installs stay lean after that: npx hyperframes init installs the core set only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have ( npx hyperframes skills update refreshes them, and never removes one); /figma , /slideshow and /remotion-to-hyperframes install on demand with npx hyperframes skills update <name> . Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back.

 Plugin packages

 Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager.
 bun run package:agent-plugin builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata,
and SHA-256 checksum. See the maintainer checklist .

 Upload to Codex

 Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed HEAD version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills:

 bun run package:codex-plugin

 This writes dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip with a hyperframes/ root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit.

 Core set

 Skill
 Use when

 /hyperframes
 Read first for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards.

 /hyperframes-cli
 The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, share, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures.

 /hyperframes-registry
 About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for hyperframes add and catalog .

 /media-use
 Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull.

 /reverse-any-video
 Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro.

 /style-sampling
 Making a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles: Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime. HyperFrames Pro.

 On demand

 Skill
 Use when

 /figma
 Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link.

 /slideshow
 A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4.

 /remotion-to-hyperframes
 Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame.

 For visual design handoff workflows, see the Claude Design guide and Open Design guide .

 Manually with the CLI

 npx hyperframes init my-video
 cd my-video
npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload
npx hyperframes render # render to MP4

 Requirements: Node.js 22+, FFmpeg

 What You Can Build

 Need ideas? Browse the Showcase for finished videos you can watch, read, run, and remix.

- Product launch videos and feature announcements

- PR walkthroughs with animated code diffs, narration, and captions

- Data visualizations, chart races, and map animations

- Social videos with kinetic captions, overlays, and music

- Docs-to-video, PDF-to-video, and site-tour explainers

- Reusable motion graphics for automated content pipelines

 Frame.md

 frame.md — your design system, ready for video.

 Every brand has a design.md . None of them were written for a camera. frame.md is the missing translation layer: it takes your web-context design spec and inverts it for the frame — the same tokens, the same rules, but rewritten so an AI agent can compose a promo video without guessing at scale or reaching for web chrome.

 The output is a DESIGN.md superset your whole toolchain can read. Atoms stay sacred. Composition stays free. Numbers come from the script.

 Biennale Yellow

 BlockFrame

 Blue Professional

 Bold Poster

 Broadside

 Capsule

 Cartesian

 Cobalt Grid

 Coral

 Creative Mode

 Browse and remix them all at hyperframes.studio/design .

 How It Works

 Define a video as HTML. Add data attributes for timing and tracks. Use GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or your own frame adapter for seekable animation.

 < div id =" stage " data-composition-id =" launch " data-start =" 0 " data-width =" 1920 " data-height =" 1080 " >
 < video
 class =" clip "
 data-start =" 0 "
 data-duration =" 6 "
 data-track-index =" 0 "
 src =" intro.mp4 "
 muted
 playsinline
 > </ video >

 < h1 id =" title " class =" clip " data-start =" 1 " data-duration =" 4 " data-track-index =" 1 " > Launch day </ h1 >

 < audio
 data-start =" 0 "
 data-duration =" 6 "
 data-track-index =" 2 "
 data-volume =" 0.5 "
 src =" music.wav "
 > </ audio >

 < script src =" https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/gsap.min.js " > </ script >
 < script >
 const tl = gsap . timeline ( { paused : true } ) ;
 tl . from ( "#title" , { opacity : 0 , y : 40 , duration : 0.8 } , 1 ) ;
 window . __timelines = window . __timelines || { } ;
 window . __timelines . launch = tl ;
 </ script >
 </ div >

 Preview instantly in the browser. Render locally or in Docker. The renderer seeks each frame in headless Chrome and encodes the result with FFmpeg, so the same input produces the same video.

 HyperFrames Stack

 HyperFrames is the open-source rendering engine, plus a growing set of tools around HTML-native video creation.

 Piece
 Status
 What it does

 CLI
 Available
 Scaffold, preview, lint, inspect, and render local video projects

 Core / Engine / Producer
 Available
 Parse compositions, drive headless Chrome, encode video, and mix audio

 Catalog
 Available
 Reusable blocks and components for transitions, overlays, captions, charts, maps, and effects

 Agent skills
 Available
 Teach coding agents the video-production patterns that generic web docs miss

 Studio
 Available, evolving
 Browser surface for previewing and editing compositions

 AWS Lambda rendering
 Available
 Deploy a distributed render stack and drive renders from your laptop or CI

 hyperframes.studio
 Available
 Community playground for previewing, iterating, sharing, and rendering HTML-native video projects

 frame.md
 Available
 Invert your design system for the camera — a DESIGN.md superset an agent can compose video from

 Catalog

 Install ready-to-use blocks and components:

 npx hyperframes add flash-through-white # shader transition
npx hyperframes add instagram-follow # social overlay
npx hyperframes add data-chart # animated chart

 Browse the catalog at hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog .

 Why HyperFrames?

- HTML-native: compositions are HTML files with data attributes. No React requirement, no proprietary timeline format.

- Agent-friendly: agents already write HTML, and the CLI is non-interactive by default.

- Deterministic: same input, same frames, same output. Built for CI, regression tests, and automated rendering.

- No build step: an index.html composition plays as-is and can be previewed directly in the browser.

- Adapter-based animation: bring GSAP, CSS animations, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or a custom runtime.

- Open source: Apache 2.0 license, with no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds.

 HyperFrames vs Remotion

 HyperFrames is inspired by Remotion . Both tools render video with headless Chrome and FFmpeg. The main difference is the authoring model: Remotion's bet is React components; HyperFrames' bet is plain HTML that humans and agents can both write easily.

 HyperFrames
 Remotion

 Authoring
 HTML + CSS + seekable animation

 Build step
 None; index.html plays as-is
 Bundler required

 Agent handoff
 Plain HTML files
 JSX / React project

 Library-clock animations
 Seekable, frame-accurate via adapters
 Wall-clock animation patterns need care

 Distributed rendering
 Local and AWS Lambda render paths

readmeText:
Sponsors

 interfaces.dev · A design engineering magazine by Jakub Krehel

 React Bits · animated React components for creative interfaces

 IMG.LY · CreativeEditor SDK

 Sent.dm · messaging APIs for SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS

 Become a sponsor

 Taste Skill ( tasteskill 2.5.1 ) is an Agent Skill that makes coding agents build professional company websites at the figma.com and x.ai level instead of assembling a generic landing page. Every build uses plain copy, one design system, one section per screen, equal left and right edges, real photographs (licensed stand-ins when the client has none), real brand icons and real product UI, a hero entrance and one or two dealt moments on every page, quiet micro-interactions, and shader effects and scroll scenes kept strictly for tech, gaming and software pages, all verified in a real browser by a checker and a finish gate that enforce the rules.

 Pages built from a single brief in earlier v2 runs:

 The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill ( credits ). Watch the launch film .

 Install

 npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill " design-taste-frontend "

 That installs the skill with the npx skills CLI.

 The skill runs its scripts with Node 22+ and an installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium (set CHROME_PATH if it is in a non-standard place). Optional: ffmpeg on the PATH, for WebP output and the phone crop of a hero photograph in photos.mjs . It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Bundled Wikimedia Commons photographs work offline; fetching additional photographs or icons uses network access.

 Claude Code plugin
 Run these inside Claude Code. The skill is namespaced under taste-skill: , so it does not collide with your other skills.

 /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill
/plugin install taste-skill@taste-skill

 /plugin update upgrades it later.

 Codex plugin
 codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill
codex plugin add taste-skill@taste-skill

 Start a new Codex session afterwards so the skill is loaded.

 From a clone, linked instead of copied
 ./install.sh symlinks the skill into Claude Code ( --codex for Codex, --all-agents for both), so a git pull updates it in place. On Windows (Git Bash) it makes a real link, or a directory junction when symlinks are not allowed, and it reports an older copied folder instead of skipping it silently.

 Already have the skill? Run the install command again; the install name did not change. Looking for one of the older skills? See Moved skills .

 How 2.5 works

 Use it by asking your agent to build or redesign a company site; the agent loads the skill, copies assets/ into the project, starts from assets/starter.html and runs the checker before it hands the page over. Every build starts by classifying the client's business ( software , gaming , tech , product , service or place ) and planning the page screen by screen before writing markup:

- Deal tokens and layout. scripts/start.mjs deals a palette made for the trade and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind ( library/palettes.json , library/type.json ), and assets/layout/deal.mjs deals a hero layout ( split , centred , product , photo , place , collage , editorial , word , film , statement or triptych ).

- Start from one system. assets/starter.html , assets/system.css and assets/layout/layout.css enforce one section per screen at desktop ( 1440x900 ), equal left and right content edges, a fixed navigation bar and a single-screen closing footer ( footer.closing ).

- Show real product UI and real photographs. Software and tech pages populate lit feature cards ( assets/ui/cards.css ) with rewritten HTML UI fragments ( assets/ui/ ) and node-and-line diagrams ( assets/diagrams/ ), with real brand and interface SVGs resolved locally by scripts/icons.mjs . Place, shop, hospitality and non-technical product pages lead with curated photographs ( scripts/photos.mjs , assets/photos/ ), typography and flat colour, crediting sources in one expandable footer line with no captions under images.

- Keep effects for tech and gaming pages. Shader grounds ( scripts/effects.mjs ), scroll scenes ( assets/scenes/ ) and procedural 3D prints ( assets/objects/ ) are dealt only on software , tech and gaming pages within a four-context WebGL cap, with static fallbacks for phones and reduced motion. Every page gets a hero entrance and one or two moments from scripts/moments.mjs ; cafes, hotels, shops, studios and services get only the photo- and type-led ones, and zero WebGL.

- Check in a real browser over HTTP. scripts/consistency.mjs , assets/layout/check.mjs , scripts/perf.mjs and scripts/shoot.mjs render the built page in headless Chrome across 1440 , 1024 , 768 and 390 , catching empty visuals, broken shaders, contrast drops, misaligned columns, section-height drift, placeholder text, invented street numbers and slow-network image gaps before the build ships. scripts/gate.mjs then holds the finish until no fixable FAIL is left, three rounds at most.

 Details of what changed from 2.1.x are in the changelog .

 The tools

 Everything is a plain Node 22+ script in the skill folder; none installs anything.

 Tool
 What it does

 scripts/start.mjs
 Deals a palette and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind and prints the <head> links and :root tokens.

 assets/layout/deal.mjs
 Deals one of eleven tested hero layouts; assets/layout/check.mjs checks it with long-headline stress tests.

 scripts/photos.mjs
 Deals vetted photographs by trade, enforces image weight and writes the one footer credit line.

 scripts/icons.mjs
 Resolves real brand and interface icons into local SVG files.

 scripts/effects.mjs , scripts/moments.mjs
 Deal shader grounds for tech, gaming and software pages, and the moments for every kind.

 scripts/gate.mjs , scripts/copy-lint.mjs
 The finish gate (also a Stop hook) and the copy linter it runs.

 scripts/consistency.mjs
 The checker: renders the page in headless Chrome over HTTP at 1440 , 1024 , 820 , 768 and 390 and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL per rule.

 scripts/perf.mjs , scripts/shoot.mjs
 Page weight and speed, and full-page and per-section screenshots.

 First run, from the project folder (a deal also arms the finish gate there): node scripts/start.mjs deal --page software (kinds: software , gaming , tech , product , service , place ). Check a built page with node scripts/consistency.mjs <url or file> --page <kind> .

 Moved skills

 This repo holds one skill, design-taste-frontend . The others moved to repos of their own and kept their install names:

 Install name
 Where it lives now

 high-end-visual-design , minimalist-ui , industrial-brutalist-ui , gpt-taste , stitch-design-taste , design-taste-frontend-v1 , design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental
 Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics

 imagegen-frontend-web , imagegen-frontend-mobile , brandkit , image-to-code
 Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills

 redesign-existing-projects
 Part of design-taste-frontend , which audits an existing page in a real browser before changing anything

 full-output-enforcement
 Removed. For the same problem, see Leonxlnx/unlazy

 Install a moved skill from its new repo under the same name:

 npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics --skill " high-end-visual-design "

 Common Questions

 What does the skill need?

Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium; ffmpeg is optional (WebP photographs and the phone crop of a hero photograph). It installs nothing and uses no API keys. Bundled Commons photographs are stored locally; network access is used only when downloading additional photographs, Google Fonts or brand icons.

 Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?

From the skill's vetted photograph library ( assets/photos/photos.json , including bundled Wikimedia Commons WebP sets and Unsplash photographs) dealt by scripts/photos.mjs . Library frames are used for trade and material details (or marked explicitly as draft stand-ins when the client has no photographs yet), never passed off as the client's own room, staff or product, and credited in one expandable footer line ( photos.mjs credits ).

 Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML?

An empty folder gets a static page from assets/starter.html . An existing React, Vue, Svelte, Astro or Tailwind project is built in its own stack, with the kit served from its public folder; a Next.js brief is built as a static export. The browser checks run on the served or built page.

 When does a page get shaders or scroll effects?

Shaders only on software , tech (technical hardware) and gaming pages, and always within a four-context WebGL budget with static phone and reduced-motion fallbacks. Places, shops, cafes, hotels, studios, services and everyday physical products stay calm: photographs, sharp typography and flat colour, with a hero entrance and one or two photo- or type-led moments in their own sections.

 Support the project

 If Taste Skill helps you, consider sponsoring:

 Feedback: open an issue or pull request, DM @lexnlin or @blueemi99 , or email hello@tasteskill.dev .

 Taste Skill has no official token, coin, or crypto project. Any token using my name, image, or project is unaffiliated and not endorsed by me.

 REA: Reverse Engineer Anything

 One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.

 See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level.

 Website · Guides · Showcases

 Quick start · How REA works · What you can analyze · Showcases · Build RL environments · FAQ · Documentation

 npx rea-agents setup

 Important
 Get REA from morluto/rea ,
 rea.tools , or the rea-agents npm package .
Follow the installation and release links from these official sources. A similar
repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official.

 Join the Reverse Engineering Community

 Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell

 See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project.

 REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion.

 Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine.

 Visit the REA website for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies.

 Quick start

 On Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron
analysis require a procps-compatible ps on REA's PATH for process ownership
checks. Recovery steps are in docs/getting-started/installation.md under
"Linux owned-process prerequisite".

 Set up your agent

 With Node.js and npm installed, run:

 npx rea-agents setup

 Choose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds
REA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing
configuration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup records the selected runtime and REA
entry script directly. If acquired through a package runner, keep its cache entry
available. Run package acquisition from a trusted directory outside the target
project. Installation and recovery details are in the setup guide below.

 Setup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and
 other agents . See
 installation and setup for provider configuration,
manual MCP registration, Claude Code/Codex plugins, and the Cursor Marketplace
plugin.

 MCP uses compact input schemas by default to reduce context overhead. Set
 REA_MCP_INPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=full in your MCP registration when you need the
complete advertised field guidance and nested validation details. Both profiles
keep the full tool set and canonical server validation. See
"Compact input schema profile" in the MCP contracts guide.

 Complete output schemas are advertised by default. If your client caps the
complete tools/list frame, set REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact to
bound each advertised output schema, or off to omit output schemas entirely.
Both settings keep canonical server-side validation and complete structured
results. See "Output schemas" in the MCP contracts guide.

 Ask your agent

 Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a
similar feature for my project.

 Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand.

 Use the terminal

 Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR:

 npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json

 The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence.
Replace the path with your target, such as "D:/apps/example" on Windows.

 To install the rea command for regular use:

 npm install --global rea-agents
rea --help

 For native analysis, configure a provider first. See the
 CLI and Evidence guide for native commands, provider selection,
snapshots and scripting.

 Update REA

 REA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your
installation up to date.

 For a CLI installed with npm install --global or bun add --global :

 rea update

 rea --update is an alias for this verified workflow and accepts the same global
output flags. Use rea update when combining it with other command controls.

 Updater commands retain at most 4 MiB of stdout and stderr combined. Oversized
metadata replies are rejected after the command exits; verbose installs continue
with bounded diagnostics. Human progress output respects terminal backpressure
and waits for submitted writes to finish.

 Bun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release,
upgrade Bun manually before running rea update .

 To refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed
by the update.

 If you use npx , update your agent setup with:

 npx rea-agents@latest setup

 Review the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands,
use npx rea-agents@latest followed by the command. With Bun, use
 bunx rea-agents@latest in place of npx rea-agents@latest .

 How REA works

 Your agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code.
REA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up
questions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation.
CLI commands use the same workflows.

 Open the full-size figure .

 What you can analyze

 REA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.23.4), 24.x (>=24.22.1), or 26.12.1+, plus npm.
Additional tools and host support depend on the target:

 Target
 What REA returns

 Desktop installations

 Pseudocode, assembly, strings, symbols, calls and references

 Saved network captures

 Engine-backed project units, artifact digests and type/method pseudo-code

 Endpoints, DNS, TLS SNI, protocol distribution and HTTP requests

representativeRepos.readmeText:
security-audit

 A coding-agent skill that turns your agent into a security auditor. It orchestrates isolated agents through reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting.

 This is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, described in Build your own vulnerability harness . The harness grew into a multi-stage, fleet-wide system; this skill is the single-repo starting point it evolved from.

 What it does

 The skill runs a structured audit in six phases:

- Reconnaissance -- map architecture, trust boundaries, input surfaces, prior evidence, and deterministic coverage in architecture.md and coverage-ledger.json .

- Coverage-led hunting -- assign isolated hunters from ledger units, record their checks, and use coverage critics to find gaps.

- Candidate validation -- give every unique candidate to a fresh verifier that tries to disprove it.

- Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .

- Independent record verification -- fresh agents verify final source claims. Material replacements receive another independent verifier.

- Target-neutral reporting -- derive REPORT.md , FINDINGS-DETAIL.md , and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md from the verified records and coverage ledger.

 The parent runs validate-coverage-ledger.cjs after creating the ledger and after each later ledger update. It runs validate-findings.cjs in Phase 4 and again after every Phase 5 replacement.

 The verdicts are distinct: confirmed has a complete source trace and bounded observed result, needs_validation has an exact unresolved fact and no severity, and rejected records a disproved candidate.

 Multiple runs against the same repo are additive. The skill uses prior ledgers and findings to target gaps, revalidate changed source, and carry forward current-source evidence without treating stale or unresolved work as covered.

 Files

 File
 Purpose

 SKILL.md
 Setup, core principles, platform terminology, workflow overview, and audit anti-patterns

 RECONNAISSANCE.md
 Phase 1 reconnaissance prompts and synthesis instructions

 HUNTING.md
 Phase 2 orchestration, hunting methodology, and validation rules

 ATTACK-CLASSES.md
 Core, wildcard, and obvious-things attack prompts

 MEMORY-SAFETY-AND-BINARY.md
 Memory-safety, binary, and kernel hunting classes for native targets

 AI-AND-LLM.md
 Prompt-injection, agent/tool, and output-handling hunting classes for LLM-backed targets

 WEB-PROTOCOL-AND-AUTH.md
 HTTP request-framing, cache, and authentication-protocol hunting classes for HTTP-protocol and auth targets

 CLIENT-SIDE.md
 DOM-injection, messaging-trust, UI-redress, and prototype-pollution hunting classes for client-side/browser targets

 SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md
 Dependency, CI, release, signing, update, plugin, and extension hunting classes

 CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md
 IAM, infrastructure-as-code, container, serverless, ingress, and runtime-configuration hunting classes

 PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md
 RPC, serialization, queue, broker, webhook, and streaming-protocol hunting classes

 RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION-AND-AVAILABILITY.md
 Shared resource, quota, queue, worker, and operator-spend hunting classes

 DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md
 Tenant isolation, cache, search, export, backup, migration, deletion, and restore hunting classes

 DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md
 Native app, deep-link, webview, exported-component, helper, daemon, and local-IPC hunting classes

 VALIDATION-AND-REPORTING.md
 Phases 3–6 candidate validation, structured output, record verification, and reporting

 report-schema.json
 JSON schema for all three findings.json verdicts

 validate-findings.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for findings.json in Phases 4 and 5

 validate-findings.test.cjs
 Findings-validator tests and producer-compatible fixture checks

 validate-coverage-ledger.cjs
 Zero-dependency validator for coverage-ledger.json in Phases 1–5

 validate-coverage-ledger.test.cjs
 Coverage-ledger validator tests

 Installation

 Install the skill with the Skills CLI :

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit

 Use --global for a user-level installation:

 npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill \
 --skill security-audit \
 --global

 Run npx skills --help for agent-selection and non-interactive options.

 Usage

 Start your coding agent in (or pointed at) the codebase you want to audit, then ask it to do a security audit:

 security audit this codebase

 find security vulnerabilities in ./src

 do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

 The skill activates automatically when the request matches its trigger (security audit, find vulnerabilities, pen-test the code, etc.). A direct codebase audit or pen-test request uses full audit mode. Security questions and focused vulnerability work use guidance mode unless you request report artifacts. In full audit mode, an unspecified output directory defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N> . The workflow writes inside the target repository only when you explicitly select a directory that version control ignores.

 Requirements

- A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents

- Node.js for the zero-dependency findings and coverage-ledger validators

- An OS-enforced sandbox for target-controlled builds, tests, processes, browsers, emulators, fuzzers, and fixtures. It must disable external networking, use a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforce resource limits, and allow writes only to assigned scratch paths. Without these controls, the workflow keeps the lead as needs_validation instead of executing target code.

 Design principles

- Only confirm established boundary failures. Keep a source-grounded blocked lead as needs_validation with its exact unresolved fact.

- Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

- Severity requires impact. Likelihood x impact, not deviation from a checklist.

- Defense-in-depth gaps are not vulnerabilities. If Layer A prevents the attack, the absence of Layer B is a hardening note.

- Multiple runs improve coverage. In our test runs, a single run found roughly half of the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total.

 Contact

 Questions, feedback, or comparing notes on AI-driven security tooling: security-ai-research@cloudflare.com

representativeRepos.readmeText:
T3 Code

 The open-source control plane for coding agents.

 Download ·
 iOS ·
 Android ·
 Web ·
 Docs ·
 Discord

 T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone.

 It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it.

 What you get

- Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to.

- Every agent in one place. Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex.

- Desktop, web, and phone. One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android.

- Remote ready. Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect .

- Git built in. Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button.

- Fast. Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug.

- Open. MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it.

 Install

 Desktop app

 Download T3 Code for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager:

 Platform
 Command

 macOS
 brew install --cask t3-code

 Windows
 winget install T3Tools.T3Code or scoop install extras/t3code

 Arch Linux
 yay -S t3code-bin

 Nix
 nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code

 Debian, Ubuntu
 .deb from Releases

 Command line

 This installs the t3 command. Run t3 to start the server and open the web app.

 curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

 On Windows, in PowerShell:

 irm https: // t3.codes / install.ps1 | iex

 To try it once without an install, run npx t3@latest .

 Phone

 Get the app from the App Store or Google Play . Then follow remote access to connect it to your computer.

 Sign in to an agent

 T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install Claude Code and run claude auth login , or install Codex CLI and run codex login .

 Provider setup has the steps for each agent. Install T3 Code covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS.

 "Wait, what are you selling me?"

 Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

 We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want.

 Documentation

- Install and first run

- Remote access from a phone or another machine

- Permission modes

- Source control

- Connect outside agents over MCP

- FAQ

 All docs has the full list.

 Contributing

 We have limited review capacity. Small, focused fixes are the most likely to be merged. Features need an approved discussion first.

- Read CONTRIBUTING.md before you report a bug or open a pull request.

- Put feature requests in Ideas .

- Build from source with the development runbook . The architecture overview explains how it works.

- Get help in Discord .

 License

 MIT

 Strategic sponsors  

   ·   Special sponsor  

 Demo workspace · Default dark theme · Watch the HD tour

 What you can do

 Voice cloning

 Turn a clean reference recording into speech in a familiar voice.

 Video dubbing

 Translate and dub videos with speech timed to the original.

 Voice design

 Describe a voice in words and generate it.

 Local models

 Choose your engines and download only the models you need.

 More screenshots

 Workspace overview

 Model packs

- Dictate & transcribe — A floating dictation widget and local transcription

- Narrate & batch — Stories, audiobooks and queued jobs

- Connect & automate — Local API, MCP, reusable recipes and watch folders

 Start with VoiceStudio (default, powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice), or pick from dozens of other engines in the Model Manager. See the features & engine catalog .

 Pro and Cloud

 Everything above is free, runs on your own hardware and needs no account. Pro and Cloud are optional.

    VoiceStudio Pro

 For paid client work across more than one machine.

 - A Commercial License for your client work, emailed to you

 - One user on up to 3 devices at once

 - Send jobs to your other GPUs while your projects stay local

 - New features and fixes first

 Closed-source build, account required, 7-day full refund. The AGPL-3.0 app stays free, including commercial use under its terms.

 See Pro plans →

    VoiceStudio Cloud

 A hosted voice and dubbing API, coming soon. No GPU needed.

 - Speech, voice design and voice cloning with consent

 - Dubbing, transcription and audiobooks

 - Usage and credits by day or project

 - Long jobs that run on their own

 Not available yet: join early access for free usage credits. The desktop app stays free and local.

 Join Cloud early access →

 Platforms

 Experimental Windows ROCm setup supports selected RDNA 2 RX 6000 GPUs with targets gfx1030 , gfx1031 or gfx1032 ; RX 6500 XT ( gfx1034 ) is excluded. GPU transcription uses a CTranslate2 build with native
 gfx1031 kernels that this repository builds from upstream source and pins by
hash, and setup checks actual GPU kernel execution. RX 6700 XT tests also cover native Torch speech generation and
PyTorch Whisper. ROCm 10 faster-whisper uses a separate inference process to
preserve safe CPU selection and fallback. Other cards and workloads retain the qualification limits in the guide.
Performance presets validate changed engine selections in an offline child
process before saving them, preserving fallback when an installed runtime fails.

 Choose your system, then expand an installation method.

 Native GGUF engines additionally support engine-specific Vulkan acceleration on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs ( OmniVoice , CosyVoice ). OmniVoice GGUF selects its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux. Vulkan discovery retries a stalled hidden probe with a native summary; Windows and Linux desktop builds fail rather than silently ship without their Vulkan module.

 NVIDIA, AMD ROCm and Compose instructions

 iPhone / iPad · IPA · sideloading

 iOS / iPadOS 17+ · Preview · On-device, offline after model download.

 Download · Guide

 Desktop and phone installers are on the latest release ; Docker images come from GHCR. No GPU? The app is fully usable on the CPU, just slower. Native GGUF engines can also use Vulkan on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs; OmniVoice GGUF picks its GPU and model size automatically on Windows and Linux ( OmniVoice , CosyVoice ). Speed by engine and hardware: performance .

 Get started

 Install using the options above. Then open Voice cloning , pick a voice or add a clean reference recording, type your text and generate. The app asks before it downloads any model.

 More install options : a specific version, current main, uninstall, from source, with a coding agent
 curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --version X.Y.Z # a specific release
curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --main # build current main
curl -fsSL https://voicestudio.sh/install | sh -s -- --uninstall # remove the app, keep your data

 If voicestudio.sh is unreachable, run the script straight from the repository:
 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio/main/scripts/install.sh | sh .
Prerequisites and behavior: installer guide .

 From source

 git clone https://github.com/debpalash/VoiceStudio.git
 cd VoiceStudio
bun run dev

 bun run dev installs the JavaScript dependencies and, when using a supported
local backend, the Python dependencies before launching Electron. Run
 bun run setup:api directly when you only need to rebuild the Python environment.

 HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows.

 The HyperFrames Studio app is free to use as well; its Pro plan adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models.

 Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run npx hyperframes skills update once, then ask your agent to make a video.

 Quick Start

 With an AI coding agent

 For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin:

 claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes
claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes

 To enable auto-update for the hyperframes marketplace, run claude in a
terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run /plugin , then select
 Marketplaces → hyperframes → Enable auto-update . Afterward, use
 /hyperframes:hyperframes . See the plugin guide
for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration.

 For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use:

 npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

 The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the Core Skills group is all you need; /slideshow , /remotion-to-hyperframes and /figma install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), npx hyperframes skills update installs exactly the core set, whereas skills add --all installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under .claude/skills / .agents/skills are excluded by default. For the full published set use npx hyperframes skills .

 skills add resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag main by hours. npx hyperframes skills update installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them.

 Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames
checkout, use npx hyperframes skills update for a global install instead: a
project-local installer target can overlap the tracked skills/ source and
overwrite uncommitted edits. See contributor setup .

 Try a prompt like:

 Using /hyperframes , create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music.

 The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills.

 Skills

 HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the /hyperframes skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first.

 For standalone installation, default to the core set ( /hyperframes , /hyperframes-cli , /hyperframes-registry , /media-use , /reverse-any-video , /style-sampling ). npx hyperframes skills update installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker ( npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without --skill installs all 9. Use npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill <name> for just one (bare name, no leading / ).

 Standalone installs stay lean after that: npx hyperframes init installs the core set only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have ( npx hyperframes skills update refreshes them, and never removes one); /figma , /slideshow and /remotion-to-hyperframes install on demand with npx hyperframes skills update <name> . Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back.

 Plugin packages

 Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager.
 bun run package:agent-plugin builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata,
and SHA-256 checksum. See the maintainer checklist .

 Upload to Codex

 Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed HEAD version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills:

 bun run package:codex-plugin

 This writes dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip with a hyperframes/ root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit.

 Core set

 Skill
 Use when

 /hyperframes
 Read first for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards.

 /hyperframes-cli
 The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, share, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures.

 /hyperframes-registry
 About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for hyperframes add and catalog .

 /media-use
 Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull.

 /reverse-any-video
 Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro.

 /style-sampling
 Making a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles: Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime. HyperFrames Pro.

 On demand

 Skill
 Use when

 /figma
 Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link.

 /slideshow
 A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4.

 /remotion-to-hyperframes
 Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame.

 For visual design handoff workflows, see the Claude Design guide and Open Design guide .

 Manually with the CLI

 npx hyperframes init my-video
 cd my-video
npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload
npx hyperframes render # render to MP4

 Requirements: Node.js 22+, FFmpeg

 What You Can Build

 Need ideas? Browse the Showcase for finished videos you can watch, read, run, and remix.

- Product launch videos and feature announcements

- PR walkthroughs with animated code diffs, narration, and captions

- Data visualizations, chart races, and map animations

- Social videos with kinetic captions, overlays, and music

- Docs-to-video, PDF-to-video, and site-tour explainers

- Reusable motion graphics for automated content pipelines

 Frame.md

 frame.md — your design system, ready for video.

 Every brand has a design.md . None of them were written for a camera. frame.md is the missing translation layer: it takes your web-context design spec and inverts it for the frame — the same tokens, the same rules, but rewritten so an AI agent can compose a promo video without guessing at scale or reaching for web chrome.

 The output is a DESIGN.md superset your whole toolchain can read. Atoms stay sacred. Composition stays free. Numbers come from the script.

 Biennale Yellow

 BlockFrame

 Blue Professional

 Bold Poster

 Broadside

 Capsule

 Cartesian

 Cobalt Grid

 Coral

 Creative Mode

 Browse and remix them all at hyperframes.studio/design .

 How It Works

 Define a video as HTML. Add data attributes for timing and tracks. Use GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or your own frame adapter for seekable animation.

 < div id =" stage " data-composition-id =" launch " data-start =" 0 " data-width =" 1920 " data-height =" 1080 " >
 < video
 class =" clip "
 data-start =" 0 "
 data-duration =" 6 "
 data-track-index =" 0 "
 src =" intro.mp4 "
 muted
 playsinline
 > </ video >

 < h1 id =" title " class =" clip " data-start =" 1 " data-duration =" 4 " data-track-index =" 1 " > Launch day </ h1 >

 < audio
 data-start =" 0 "
 data-duration =" 6 "
 data-track-index =" 2 "
 data-volume =" 0.5 "
 src =" music.wav "
 > </ audio >

 < script src =" https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/gsap.min.js " > </ script >
 < script >
 const tl = gsap . timeline ( { paused : true } ) ;
 tl . from ( "#title" , { opacity : 0 , y : 40 , duration : 0.8 } , 1 ) ;
 window . __timelines = window . __timelines || { } ;
 window . __timelines . launch = tl ;
 </ script >
 </ div >

 Preview instantly in the browser. Render locally or in Docker. The renderer seeks each frame in headless Chrome and encodes the result with FFmpeg, so the same input produces the same video.

 HyperFrames Stack

 HyperFrames is the open-source rendering engine, plus a growing set of tools around HTML-native video creation.

 Piece
 Status
 What it does

 CLI
 Available
 Scaffold, preview, lint, inspect, and render local video projects

 Core / Engine / Producer
 Available
 Parse compositions, drive headless Chrome, encode video, and mix audio

 Catalog
 Available
 Reusable blocks and components for transitions, overlays, captions, charts, maps, and effects

 Agent skills
 Available
 Teach coding agents the video-production patterns that generic web docs miss

 Studio
 Available, evolving
 Browser surface for previewing and editing compositions

 AWS Lambda rendering
 Available
 Deploy a distributed render stack and drive renders from your laptop or CI

 hyperframes.studio
 Available
 Community playground for previewing, iterating, sharing, and rendering HTML-native video projects

 frame.md
 Available
 Invert your design system for the camera — a DESIGN.md superset an agent can compose video from

 Catalog

 Install ready-to-use blocks and components:

 npx hyperframes add flash-through-white # shader transition
npx hyperframes add instagram-follow # social overlay
npx hyperframes add data-chart # animated chart

 Browse the catalog at hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog .

 Why HyperFrames?

- HTML-native: compositions are HTML files with data attributes. No React requirement, no proprietary timeline format.

- Agent-friendly: agents already write HTML, and the CLI is non-interactive by default.

- Deterministic: same input, same frames, same output. Built for CI, regression tests, and automated rendering.

- No build step: an index.html composition plays as-is and can be previewed directly in the browser.

- Adapter-based animation: bring GSAP, CSS animations, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI, or a custom runtime.

- Open source: Apache 2.0 license, with no per-render fees or commercial-use thresholds.

 HyperFrames vs Remotion

 HyperFrames is inspired by Remotion . Both tools render video with headless Chrome and FFmpeg. The main difference is the authoring model: Remotion's bet is React components; HyperFrames' bet is plain HTML that humans and agents can both write easily.

 None; index.html plays as-is

 Library-clock animations
 Seekable, frame-accurate via adapters
 Wall-clock animation patterns need care

 Distributed rendering

Claude SEO

 Free, open-source SEO audits inside Claude Code .

 Rank higher in Google and get cited by AI search.
